konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the reported first half and the subsidiary's own plan, not on a fade. The first half, reported through S6 (which describes the interim as audited; the LK itself is not archived), ran revenue at USD 1.77bn, up 34.0%, with coal up 29.8% and technology up 89.3% [S6]; the listed coal subsidiary's own covered model carries FY2026E revenue up 33% on the 58Mt plan and the house coal deck's FY2026E marker (137.0 against 108.4 in FY2025) [S20, S12, F48]. Coal is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue [S9, F7], so a 30% consolidated step is the subsidiary-consistent path and is the revenue-growth clamp for this template. FY2027E falls 14% for a sourced reason, not a hand-set fade: the same subsidiary model and deck carry the FY2027E coal marker 14% below FY2026E on a flat 58Mt volume [S20]. From FY2028E the top line is held at the FY2027E level because no source supports a further decline; the path feeds only the small earnings cross-checks and does not set the target, which is the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Follows the covered coal subsidiary's own modelled gross margin, because the subsidiary is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue and holding last year's ratio against a 26% higher FY2026E coal marker would be the unsourced squeeze the most-likely rule forbids [S9, S20]. The subsidiary's model carries FY2026E gross margin of 40.7% (FY2025A 31.9%), fading to 34.5% in FY2027E and 31.2% in FY2028E on the house coal deck's marker path (137.0 then 118.0) [S20]. DSSA's own FY2025A consolidated gross margin was 33.7% against the subsidiary's 31.9%, so the group carries a small non-coal premium; we use the subsidiary's ratios directly rather than add one, which leaves the forecast slightly below the group's own FY2025A relationship. From FY2028E the ratio is held at the last modelled year — no source supports a further move.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of SG&A and other operating expense to revenue [S0], held flat in real terms. The group's overhead carries the technology, chemicals and corporate functions as well as the mine, and nothing in the LK sources a step down; a decline would be an unsourced haircut.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the group reports consolidated D&A of USD 78.2m for FY2025 and USD 83.6m for FY2024 in the segment note [F17, F18], roughly three times the pack's direct-method figure, and the ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast carries. The pack's D&A is small because the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of capital spending to revenue [S0, S9], held flat. The group spends across the mine, the power assets, the broadband network and the data-centre build, and that spending absorbed essentially all of group EBITDA in the recent audited years; the ratio is the witnessed rate, not a target, and no source supports cutting it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 30 June 2026 balance sheet already shows the release: operating working capital stood at USD 477.8m against USD 610.8m at the FY2025A year-end [S0, latest_bs 2026-06-30], after the audited first half [S6]. Holding that dollar level — not the three-year average ratio, which the FY2023 commodity peak distorts — makes FY2026E NWC fall to USD 477.8m and then stay flat, so the FCFF release is the one already visible on the reported balance sheet rather than a second, unsourced assumption. Every later year's ratio is set to reproduce the same USD 477.8m at that year's revenue.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A effective rate of 5.87% (interest expense USD 71.37m on opening debt USD 1,216.33m) rather than the three-year average of 6.66%, which carries the FY2023 rate when debt was much smaller. The last actual is the sourced rate on the current debt stack [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at the engine default (no new borrowing) with the caveat stated in the report rather than a fabricated financing plan: the LK says only that long-term bank borrowings may rise in the next few years to fund new projects and that the group funds capex from internal cash first, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9], which is not a number we can date. On this method the forecast balance sheet feeds only the small earnings and book cross-checks, not the target, so an unsourced debt schedule would add false precision. Where the modelled cash path runs thin past the forecast horizon the report says so plainly [S9].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025A actual of USD 44.157m rather than the engine's zero default: the last audited year earned a positive other non-operating line and nothing in the FY2025 accounts or the H1-2026 release sources a step to zero. Carrying the last actual is the most-likely rule; zeroing it was an unsourced haircut that depressed FY2026E parent profit below the reported first half [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A actual ratio of 36.18% (minority interest USD 130.662m on net profit USD 361.20m) rather than the three-year average of 43.33%, which is inflated by FY2023 when the coal subsidiary earned a peak-year profit. The most-likely rule is to reproduce the last audited year's split; the three-year average quietly raised the minority cut by seven points and pushed FY2026E parent profit below the reported H1-2026 actual [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission: the group's policy permits a distribution of up to 30% of net profit [F14], but the accounts record no dividend payment in any reported year [S0, S9] and the company states it has not distributed dividends because its subsidiaries require substantial capital expenditure [S9]. A payout we cannot source, on a name that has never paid one, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a sum of the parts with a holding-company discount, so no perpetual growth rate reaches the target; this input only frames the cross-checks. It is set at the house's long-run USD inflation assumption, below the house cap for a USD-reporting name, because a coal-heavy conglomerate should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Charged at the wide end of the house holdco band, on the card's dividend-upstream law rather than on a hope of narrowing. The base rate for holdco and SOTP names is that a discount of 20-40% persists indefinitely, and a narrower discount needs a NAMED, DATED catalyst that actually upstreams cash. The parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders and states that it keeps the capital in its subsidiaries because they need the spending [S9]; that is the card's definition of a holdco that deserves the widest discount in its range. The two capital-return precedents — the 2023 buyback of 154,105,327 shares for USD 483.8m, part reissued in 2024 [S9, F44, F45], and the Rp1tn buyback running from 19 October 2026 to 18 January 2027 [S28] — are small against market value (the live one is about a hundredth of it) and neither is a recurring distribution, so neither passes the dated-upstream test. The peer distribution is measured, not asserted: the house CONGLOMERATES comps put ADRO, BRPT, CUAN and FOLK at 30%, ASII at 30%, TOBA at 40%, BNBR at 38%, BHIT at 40% and IMJS at 60%, so the median and the mode are both 30% and 40% is the wide end of the band, not its middle. We charge 40% because the hoarding law, not the peer median, sets this name's warranted discount: the parent receives the subsidiary's dividends and passes none on. The governance file — related-party purchases of family property, telecom and insurance, the data-centre package bought from a family affiliate, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67] — widens it further and is NOT the OJK trading sanction; the OJK manipulation finding is assigned once, to the konglo lens (enforcement_manipulation), per the konglo card, and is not counted again here. The 2023 and 2026 buybacks are the only evidence against the widest end, and they do not carry a distribution.

challenges.challenge: The 51% GEMS stake is marked at the subsidiary's house target of Rp6,660.51 (F83, tp_final) instead of its house fundamental twelve-month value of Rp6,093.72 (F100, tp_fundamental). The konglo card, as reconciled 5 Nov 2026, requires a covered listed subsidiary to be marked at its pre-lens fundamental "so that no sibling regime premium enters the parent's fundamental value; the parent's own konglo lens is applied once, after the SOTP", and states in terms that the earlier "house target" wording would carry the sibling's lens twice. Section four asserts the opposite as house law, and fund record labels F83 "used to mark DSSA's 51% stake". The GEMS mark is therefore 9.3% above the value the card requires, overstating the parent's largest part by roughly USD 96m — about 5% of the fundamental and about Rp25 of the target (446 toward roughly 420-423). The SELL survives; the stated method and the target do not.
challenges.answer: Corrected in this revision. The GEMS stake now enters the SOTP at the subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental twelve-month value, not its post-lens house target: the holding is marked at 51% x F100 (Rp6,093.716828) x 5,882.353m shares over the house USD/IDR of 18,140, and F83 is retained only as a reference fact. Section four now states the 5 Nov 2026 reconciliation and the bias-and-tone rationalisation is removed; the target re-runs to Rp441 from the prior Rp446. The peer-discount line was also corrected to ASII at 30% (the house comps value), not 25%.

challenges.challenge: The engine bear (180, a 50% discount shock) is materially milder than the bear the report itself describes: at the subsidiary's own published bear target the controlling stake is worth about a third of its base mark, and a 10% haircut to the two book marks takes the parent's fundamental down roughly two-fifths. That asset tail is disclosed in prose but is not in the value being weighted, while the 30% bear probability is explicitly calibrated by reference to it ("it is why the bear weight is 30% rather than lower"). The weighted fundamental of 214 therefore combines a bear probability sized for a severity that the bear value excludes. If the bear carried the two-fifths lower fundamental the report describes, the weighted value would fall by roughly 7% and the target to about 415 — the same direction as C1 but from a separate cause.
challenges.answer: Disclosed rather than smuggled into the shock. Section five now states that the 30% weight is set against the discount-only bear value in the table, not the conditional asset tail, and that capitalising the tail would take the probability-weighted fundamental about a tenth below the modelled fundamental and the target below the modelled target. The engine's SOTP cannot re-price the covered holding inside a DSSA scenario, so the tail is stated at full strength instead of being forced into a discount shock that would misstate it.

challenges.challenge: Restitution is correctly left out of the base because S31 names no amount, timing or payer. But the report never tests the one payer path its own evidence establishes: on the administrative leg OJK confirmed "bukan ketiga emiten itu yang membayar denda, tetapi pihak-pihak terkait emiten" — PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, the 59.9% controlling shareholder, paid the Rp1.5tn. A restitution pool of unknown size levied on the same controller is a funding call on the shareholder of a name whose float is 21.5%, and the konglo card says float and controller flows set the marginal price. The report also records a checked absence for a pledge of the controller's DSSA stake but never connects it to this cash call.
challenges.answer: The payer route is now tested in section five: issuer, controller and brokers. It records that the administrative fines were paid by the related parties and that the named recipient was PT Sinar Mas Tunggal [S21, S26]; that a restitution levy on the controller is a funding call on the shareholder of a thin-float name, with the checked absence of a pledge of the controller's DSSA stake and of any disclosed stake sale or margin call [S9, F74]; and that the controller route would widen the discount warrant without adding a second lens flag, because the enforcement flag is already counted.

challenges.challenge: The update is framed as a 5 November statement ("On 5 November 2026 the regulator said", "On 5 November it added", "the 5 November restitution statement") in six places, including the investment summary and the lens discussion. S31's text places the quotes at a press briefing: "ujar Agus kepada wartawan, di Media Gathering BEI, Mandalika, Sabtu, (31/10/2026)". The article was published on 5 November; the regulator spoke on 31 October. F109-F111 are tagged 2026-11-05 without distinguishing the statement date from the publication date.
challenges.answer: The statement is now dated 31 October 2026 at the BEI Media Gathering in Mandalika and the article to 5 November, in the summary, sections five, six and seven and the catalyst list; F110 and F111 are tagged 31 October. The only remaining 5 November references are the article's publication date and the konglo card's reconciliation date.

challenges.challenge: gross_margin for FY2026E is set at 40.7%, the covered subsidiary's own modelled gross margin, and applied to consolidated revenue of 3,628.6. The coal arm is 89.1% of group revenue (2,487.6 of 2,791.2), so the remaining technology and chemicals lines — a low-margin distribution book and a captive power business with no external revenue — are implicitly credited with the same 40.7% margin. The group's own FY2025A margin of 33.7% is consistent with coal at a lower price and thinner non-coal margins; capturing the full 7pp subsidiary margin step at group level overstates FY2026E gross profit by roughly 2-2.5 points of revenue and the reported EBITDA of 875. It does not reach the target, but it drives the calibration gate justification and the first-half bridge.
challenges.answer: The premise that the non-coal parts are thinner-margin is contradicted by the segment note. In FY2025A the coal column earned F114 of segment result on F112 of revenue, while the non-coal columns earned F115 less F114 on F113 less F112, a higher margin. Applying the subsidiary's 40.7% to all group revenue therefore understates, not overstates, the non-coal contribution; the FY2026E EBITDA is conservative on this line, not overstated. Facts F112-F115 carry the verbatim segment-note rows, the report adds the arithmetic, and the calibration justification records the check.

challenges.challenge: Section five is careful to state that the business and regime scenario sets are combined under the independence convention and that the joint-bear weight is the product of 30% and 25%, with the honest observation that positive correlation makes it more likely. The mirror is absent: the joint-bull path (25% business bull at 252 with the regime bull at 704, a 6.25% product under the same convention) is never stated, so a reader cannot see the upside the convention actually assigns. The same positive correlation the report says makes the joint bear likelier applies to the joint bull.
challenges.answer: The joint-bull path is now stated alongside the joint-bear under the same independence convention: the business bull at val.scenarios.bull.tp with the regime bull at val.konglo.scenarios.bull.tp, at a weight that is the product of the two branch probabilities, with the same positive-correlation caveat applied to the upside. The convention is no longer disclosed only on the downside.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull side is largely present (MSCI Standalone rejection by 30 Jun 2027 lifting the index-increase freeze, refloat as the route off HSC, the Rp1tn buyback as a dated catalyst, technology revenue +89% in H1). But the report takes care to state the joint-bear path under the independence convention and never states the joint-bull path (25% business x 25% regime) or its value, so the upside tail is disclosed less than the downside one [S0, S20].

missing_bear_case.note: Two gaps. (1) The engine bear (180) is a holdco-discount-only shock, while the report itself says the asset tail takes the parent's fundamental down roughly two-fifths; the 30% bear weight is justified by a downside that is not in the value being weighted, so the probability-weighted 214 is internally inconsistent [S20, S9]. (2) Restitution is left as an issuer-side tail even though the administrative leg was paid by PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, so a repeat controller cash call and its supply/pledge route to a 21.5%-float name is never considered [S21, S26, S31].

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are individually sourced: GEMS mark from the subsidiary's model, power and technology at audited net book, holdco discount 40% from the dividend-upstream law. The forecast, however, applies GEMS's 40.7% FY2026E gross margin to 100% of group revenue when the coal arm is 89%, which overstates group gross profit by roughly two points of revenue and the FY2026E EBITDA of 875 [S9, S20].

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks pass: S21 says Rp2.1tn paid, the Rp1.5tn DSSA share and that the parties, not the issuers, paid; S30 lists 81 names including DSSA and GEMS from 2 Nov 2026; S31 carries F109-F111 verbatim. Two defects: the statement is dated 5 Nov in six places although S31's quote is from Agus on Saturday 31 Oct 2026; and the discount basis puts ASII at 25% when the comps table shows 30% [S0].

valuation_method_fit.note: SOTP is the right primary method and the P/E and P/BV are correctly dropped on a manipulated tape. But the largest part is marked at the subsidiary's post-lens house target (6,660.5) rather than its pre-lens fundamental (6,093.7), which is exactly the double-count the konglo card's 5 Nov 2026 reconciliation forbids; see C1. The reverse-DCF answer is honestly reported as a premium rather than a discount.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is measured and the SELL is evidence-driven by the lens rather than by tone. One rationalisation: section four asserts that carrying the child's konglo premium is "the card's group consistency rule" when the card says the opposite, so a bearish conclusion is defended with a method that actually flatters it — the error runs against the report's own direction.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the coal deck markers (137.0 FY2026E, 118.0 normalised), USD reporting, 12.6% COE and 10.7% WACC, all within the CONGLOMERATES peer range (ADRO 13.3%/10.6%, ASII HOLD). Royalty and permit terms arrive through the GEMS model rather than a second forecast, as the card allows.

conservatism_audit.note: Every below-actual input is sourced: cost of debt 5.87% (last actual, not the 6.66% average), other non-operating held at 44.2, minority at the FY2025A 36.2%, payout zero on a documented no-dividend record, discount 40% justified on the upstream law rather than assumed. The only unsourced asymmetry is the bear value against the stated asset tail, captured in C2.

calibration.note: cov_engine qc shows no blocking flags: the +7.0pp EBITDA margin and -9.5pp gross margin drift are both justified with S20 and S9, and both WARN flags are answered. The +7pp justification still inherits the group-margin scope issue in C5, which should be stated.

signoff.notes: APPROVED at sign-off (update v17, round 1). QC PASS with no BLOCK and the judge PASS neutral. The round-1 FATAL is answered on substance: the 51% GEMS stake now enters the SOTP at the subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental twelve-month value (F100, Rp6,093.716828), not its post-lens house target (F83, Rp6,660.51), so no sibling regime premium is carried inside the parent's fundamental and the parent's konglo lens is applied once after the SOTP - the VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 reconciliation of 5 November 2026. The lens reads correctly: fundamental 12-month value 206, price 3.41x that value, premium kept 2.135, target 441, TR -29.5%; the regime flags (hsc +0.05, enforcement_manipulation +0.1) are the konglo deck's parameters, not the analyst's. Group consistency holds: GEMS is covered and marked at its pre-lens fundamental, no sibling sits at market or at a lens target, and the free float of 21.46% clears the 15% minimum (registry ff_rule, konglo-deck S25). Lint draft PASS. The one open FIX (Q1) is a provenance error, not an analytical one: sections 1 and 6 say the konglo registry's free-float source points at the GEMS interim article and that a correction is open with the Director, but the registry's ff_rule.source is the konglo-deck S25 (the BEI free-float release, "DSSA Sudah Memenuhi"), not the ticker's S25, and the 21.46% comes from the IDX-IC mirror/datapack [S0]; the registry is not wrong and there is nothing for the Director to correct. No lens input or target changes, so it is carried as a recorded condition for the next version rather than a RETURN. Also carried, non-blocking: Q2 (F100 is the GEMS v4 snapshot; the live fundamental is Rp6,146.56, so the USD1,007.8m mark is 0.9-2.0% stale - refresh at the next version), Q3 (the assumptions note still cites the pre-C1 gross parts of USD2,554.45m against the engine's USD2,460.72m), Q4 (add per-component USD m marks to the section 4 table), the 9,254-word length against the 3,500 update ceiling (trim at the next version), and the single-method warning (P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted, because they are struck on the tape OJK found manipulated - justified, but the house standard asks for two cross-checks). Batch bias check, CONGLOMERATES: ratings are mixed (ABMM ADD, ADRO/BNBR/IMJS/TOBA HOLD, BRPT REDUCE, DSSA/FOLK SELL, BHIT parked BUY, CUAN parked SELL, ZBRA NOT RATED), so there is no same-side tilt; DSSA's 40% discount is the top of the card's band and ASII's 21.83% the observed low, but they rest on different mechanisms (dividend-upstream law vs observed market-implied) and both are reasoned, so the spread is not a shared input. The SELL comes from the price sitting 3.41x the parts, not from a deck path: WACC 10.7% and COE 12.6% sit mid-peer. No position, sizing or P&L recorded.

bias.note: Neither direction is unsourced. The 40% holdco discount is the wide end of the house band but is tied to the documented zero-dividend/hoarding record [S9, F14] and the card's dividend-upstream law; the coal stake is the sibling's pre-lens fundamental, below its quote [S20, F100]; the below-actual cost of debt (5.87%) and minority split (36.2%) are the last audited actuals, not haircuts. The bear and bull mirror the same driver (holdco discount +10pp / -10pp) and base is 45%. The one residual is disclosed rather than stacked: the 30% bear weight is set against a discount-only bear while the conditional asset tail is stated separately [S20, S9]. No unsourced optimism or conservatism found.

findings.finding: Sections 1 and 6 say the konglo registry's free-float source field points at the GEMS interim article (the ticker's S25) and that a correction is open with the Director. That is a namespace error: the registry's free-float entry is regime.ff_rule.source = konglo-deck S25 (fund record), the BEI free-float release that lists DSSA at 15% and "Telah Memenuhi"; the 21.46% lens input comes from the IDX-IC mirror/datapack [S0]. The registry is not wrong and the Director has nothing to correct.

S20 is the GEMS v4 snapshot (30 Oct 2026) with tp_fundamental Rp6,093.716828 (F100). The live GEMS model now gives Rp6,146.56 and its 1 Nov QC record Rp6,215, so the parent's USD1,007.8m mark is 0.9-2.0% stale. Immaterial to the call, but the card asks for the sibling's current house value.

The Non-GEMS minority holding note in fund record still cites a "gross parts value of USD2,554.45m"; that is the pre-C1 figure at GEMS's post-lens target (Rp6,660.51). The engine's current gross value is USD2,460.72m, so the note contradicts the model.

Section 4's holdings table lists the parts and mark bases but no per-component values; the holdco card's output contract asks for SOTP/share with per-component marks. The values are computable from the prose (F23-F34, F41) but not shown in the table.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +7.0pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2026E is priced at the house coal deck's FY2026E marker (137.0 against 108.4 in FY2025A) and at the covered GEMS model's own FY2026E gross margin of 40.7%, so the roughly seven-point EBITDA margin step is the subsidiary's price-driven forecast, not an unsourced margin squeeze; the coal arm is about nine-tenths of group revenue [S20, S12, S9]. The group-wide ratio is conservative on the non-coal parts: the segment note shows the non-coal columns' FY2025A segment result over revenue above the coal column's margin, so applying the subsidiary's ratio to all group revenue does not overstate them [S9, F112-F115].

flags.justification: The taper follows the covered subsidiary's modelled gross margin path — 40.7% in FY2026E, 34.5% in FY2027E and 31.2% in FY2028E — on the house coal deck's marker normalisation from 137.0 to 118.0, and the ratio is held at 31.2% from FY2028E onward; no further move is assumed [S20].
